However, more recent reports have shown that the statements have not stopped many Romariians from joining the militia.

At the same time, the Christian militia (which controls most of the western parts of the country), the Christendom of Romariia, has intensified its displacements of muslims within territories under its control, with the group claiming it is protecting Christians from suffering the same fate as those in Lil Geranora and Warszawa.

In response to the growing instability, the Government has formally requested cooperation from Arelia, proposing joint patrols in regions of both nations near the former territories of Wielka Warszawa and Geranora to contain the spread of violence and prevent cross-border escalation.

Experts warn that the sudden emergence of another armed faction, especially a religious one, combined with ongoing separatist unrest, existing militia activity, and international pressure, marks a dangerous turning point in the crisis.

.
 
A população indígena de Bravanor representa 3,2% de toda população nacional, centrados especialmente nas regiões norte e oeste, povos como os Charruas, Kaingangs, yanomamis etc...
Embora haja desigualdades sim, a voz dos povos indígenas é ouvida, por exemplo:
O Estatuto Nacional dos Povos Originários (ENPO) definiu algumas cláusulas importantes:
[i]Consultas obrigatórias do Senado e Câmara dos Deputados com representantes indígenas em decisões que afetam comunidades originárias.[/i]
 ....
Além disso o ENPO definiu a concessão econômica de milhões de reais desde sua fundação em 1981 às comunidades indígenas para compensar a tomada de terras da Lei da Posse Livre de 1805, que essencialmente dava total direito dos colonos de tomarem terras dos povos nativos e "civilizar" Ou os matar para tomar a terra, note que as compensações so se efetivaram de fato a partir da década de 1990, o ENPO também é um estatuto que não pode ser alterado por meios convencionais simples no legislativo, quaisquer alteração nele EXIGE por direito constitucional,  o consentimento e participação indígena.
O próprio judiciário imperial impede que o governo atropele os direitos indígenas e explode terras como bem desejar, já que o judiciário tem o direito pleno de conter essas políticas de serem implementadas por quanto tempo for necessário até a consulta indígena ser feita de forma esperada pela ENPO. Esse sistema funciona como forma de segurar contradições do Senado.
Há também a [i]Secretaria de saúde indígena,[/i] organização essa que é um sistema público de saúde dedicado mais aos povos originários que trabalha com organizações originárias e respeita medicina tradicional.
É definido pelo ENPO que embora o governo imperial tenha 
 Domínio inalienável da terras dos indígenas, a possessão indígena propriamente dita é direito inalienável deles, os recursos na terra também, a terra indígena não pode ser vendida ou tomada por quaisquer identidade.
A educação escolar indígena é algo tem desde 2020 sendo mais desenvolvido no império, desde esse ano tem.sido criadas, especificamente no norte e oeste onde escolas são lecionadas totalmente em línguas indígenas.
Contudo apesar de tudo isso a representação política dos povos originários é quase nula já que não há nenhum assento especial ou quaisquer representante indígena no legislativo, embora candidatos tenham competido mais nos últimos anos, nunca chegaram a ser representados no legislativo.
[i][b]A Marcha das cadeiras Vazias.[/b][/i]
19 de Agosto de 2024.
Coincidência ou não, na mesma época em que os protestos pela democratização iniciaram no império, se iniciariam também protestos pela representação indígena no Senado Imperial, mais de 35 mil apoiadores do [i]Movimento Cadeiras vazias [/i](MCV) como é conhecido popularmente (embora não tenha tido uma nomeação oficial de fato), formado pelos próprios povos indígenas, apoiadores não indigenas, artistas e intelectuais liderados pela yanomami Yasmin Carunê,  todos os indígenas trouxeram consigo cadeiras, e as deixaram dispostas em frente ao prédio do senado imperial por 1 hora, mas, não se sentaram em nenhuma, Carunê então explicou em frente a todos ali presentes e para o Senado.
[i]"Trouxemos cada um de nossas terras, cadeiras, caminhamos por dias levando essas cadeiras conosco, mas no final não nos sentamos, por que vocês se perguntam? A resposta está na contradição do governo. Desde que a ENPO foi promulgada entramos numa longa jornada pelos direitos de nossos povos originários, mas essa longa jornada, terminou em nenhuma cadeira para nos representar."[/i]
Ela então passou palavra para Gustavo Charok, um professor descendente dos poucos charruas que ainda vivem, suas palavras foram curtas, mas carregadas.
"Deem-nos direitos, deem-nos voz, deem-nos assento.
Nos deram Quarenta e três anos de espera, deem-nos representação, ou negamos esta nação ."
A resposta vinda do Primeiro Ministro Gaspar de Souza, veio logo em seguida, quando ele saiu do prédio do Senado e em frente aos manifestantes, falou em um tom calmo.
"O Senado respeita o direito à manifestação pacífica e reconhece a relevância das demandas apresentadas. Estaremos abertos a mais diálogos se forem do desejo de vós."
Dentro do senado já porém, havia alguns questionamentos, o senador de Campo Novino, Rafael Barcelos, do LP abriu a seguinte questão, nos bastidores;
"Eles não estão pedindo terras. Estão pedindo cadeiras. Dar a eles uma voz no Senado é mais barato do que explicar ao mundo por que reprimimos uma mãe yanomami."
[b]Resultados: [/b]
A imprensa falou muito sobre os protestos pelo jornal e pela televisão, em especial à fala de Gustavo Charok que virou manchete de jornal, 
[u][i]"Deem-nos representação ou negamos esta nação."[/i][/u]
No dia seguinte Yasmin Carunê enviou ao senado uma carta, ou petição, exigindo, em resumo:
Criação de 5 cadeiras no Senado imperial para cada região que seja dada para representar os povos indígenas, e 7 na Câmara dos Deputados.
Criação de um ministério próprio aos povos originários.
Etc...
O imperador em um gesto simbólico mas privado, convidou Yasmin Carunê para um chá no Palácio da Fênix imperial para discutir melhor sobre a proposta dela ao senado, segundo Yasmin o imperador discutiu de um modo surpreendentemente liberal sobre os direitos indígenas em Bravanor.
[Spoiler=Translation]
.

The indigenous population of Bravanor represents 3.2% of the entire national population, concentrated especially in the northern and western regions, peoples such as the Charruas, Kaingangs, Yanomamis, etc...
Although there are inequalities, the voice of indigenous peoples is heard, for example:
The National Statute of Indigenous Peoples (ENPO) defined some important clauses:
[i]Mandatory consultations of the Senate and Chamber of Deputies with indigenous representatives in decisions that affect native communities.[/i]

...
In addition, the ENPO defined the economic concession of millions of reais since its foundation in 1981 to indigenous communities to compensate for the land grabbing under the Free Possession Law of 1805, which essentially gave colonists the total right to take land from native peoples and "civilize" or kill them to take the land. Note that the compensations only actually took effect from the 1990s onwards. The ENPO is also a statute that cannot be altered by simple conventional means in the legislature; any alteration to it REQUIRES By constitutional right, indigenous consent and participation.
The imperial judiciary itself prevents the government from trampling on indigenous rights and exploding lands as it pleases, since the judiciary has the full right to contain these policies from being implemented for as long as necessary until the indigenous consultation is carried out in the manner expected by the ENPO. This system functions as a way to contain contradictions from the Senate.
There is also the [i]Indigenous Health Secretariat,[/i] an organization that is a public health system dedicated more to native peoples that works with native organizations and respects traditional medicine.
It is defined by the ENPO that although the imperial government has

Inalienable dominion over indigenous lands, the indigenous possession itself is their inalienable right, as are the resources on the land; indigenous land cannot be sold or taken by any entity.

Indigenous school education has been more developed in the empire since 2020, and since that year, schools have been created, specifically in the north and west, where schools are taught entirely in indigenous languages.
However, despite all this, the political representation of indigenous peoples is almost nonexistent, as there are no special seats or any indigenous representatives in the legislature. Although there have been more candidates competing in recent years, they have never been represented in the legislature.

[i][b]The March of the Empty Chairs.[/b][/i]
August 19, 2024.
Coincidence or not, at the same time that protests for democratization began in the empire, protests for indigenous representation in the Imperial Senate also began. More than 35,000 supporters of the [i]Empty Chairs Movement[/i] (MCV), as it is popularly known (although it did not have an official name), formed by the indigenous peoples themselves, non-indigenous supporters, artists and intellectuals led by the Yanomami Yasmin Carunê, all brought chairs with them and left them arranged in front of the Imperial Senate building for 1 hour, but did not sit in any of them. Carunê then explained this in front of everyone present and to the Senate.

[i]"We brought each of our lands, chairs, we walked for days carrying these chairs with us, but in the end we didn't sit down, why do you ask? The answer lies in the contradiction of the government. Since the ENPO was enacted, we have embarked on a long journey for the rights of our native peoples, but this long journey ended in no chair to represent us."[/i]
She then passed the word to Gustavo Charok, a professor descended from the few Charrua who are still alive, his words were short but loaded.
"Give us rights, give us a voice, give us a seat.
You gave us forty-three years of waiting, give us representation, or we reject this nation."
The response from Prime Minister Gaspar de Souza came soon after, when he left the Senate building and, in front of the demonstrators, spoke in a calm tone.
"The Senate respects the right to peaceful demonstration and recognizes the relevance of the demands presented. We will be open to further dialogue if you so desire."
Inside the Senate, however, there were already some questions. Senator Rafael Barcelos, from Campo Novino, of the LP party, raised the following issue behind the scenes:

"They are not asking for land. They are asking for seats. Giving them a voice in the Senate is cheaper than explaining to the world why we repressed a Yanomami mother."

[b]Results:[/b]
The press talked a lot about the protests in newspapers and on television, especially Gustavo Charok's speech, which became a newspaper headline:
[u][i]"Give us representation or we deny this nation."[/i][/u]
The following day, Yasmin Carunê sent a letter, or petition, to the Senate, demanding, in short:
The creation of 5 seats in the Imperial Senate for each region designated to represent Indigenous peoples, and 7 in the Chamber of Deputies.

Creation of a ministry specific to the original peoples.
Etc...
The emperor, in a symbolic but private gesture, invited Yasmin Carunê for tea at the Imperial Phoenix Palace to further discuss her proposal to the senate. According to Yasmin, the emperor discussed indigenous rights in Bravanor in a surprisingly liberal manner.[/spoiler]

[b]An Interrupted Meeting 2:[/b]

After the police had cleared the scene, Alexei Malenkova would take a walk. It was the late evening, and instead of heading straight to the train station to return home, he would stop by a bar.

At this bar was a disheartened 29 year old. He had just blown a very important meeting, and was on drink number nine to cope. His head was spinning with awful thoughts, about flying off the handle, what he should have done differently; and in walked the man with whom he'd met earlier.

He stumbled up to him, thought he said some words, but they didn't really cut through the fog. Then all he saw was red, red for his people, red in his vision, Red on the ground. Red around his handcuffed wrists, red on his face in the mirror.

And later he calmed down, and his world turned to blue. The blue-metal sheen of the chair and the table, the blue of an officers uniform. Blue like the feelings he held in his heart, blue like the lights on the car that brought him there. Blue, like the chance he blew for a peaceful solution by killing Red in cold, drunk blood.
